sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's explore how constructors help create objects in Java - like giving life to your code!

• What constructors are and why they're essential
• How to write and use constructors
• The magic of default vs. custom constructors

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine constructors as a factory assembly line for objects. When you order a pizza (create an object), the constructor is like the chef who:

• Takes your order (parameters)
• Prepares the base (initializes fields)
• Adds your toppings (sets values)
• Delivers your perfect pizza (returns the object)

In Java, constructors are special methods that:
• Have the same name as the class
• Don't have a return type (not even void)
• Are called automatically when you use 'new'

Key Points
points: A constructor has the same name as its class and no return type
Constructors are called automatically when an object is created with new
A no-arg constructor initializes fields to default values
A parameterized constructor accepts arguments to set initial field values
If you define any constructor, Java no longer provides a default no-arg constructor

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Constructors are special methods that create and initialize objects. They run automatically when you use the 'new' keyword. Practice writing constructors to get comfortable with object creation. Ready to learn about method overloading next.

questions.question: What is a constructor in Java?
options: A special method that initializes objects when they are created
A method that returns the class name
A static method in every class
questions.explanation: A constructor is a special method called when an object is created using 'new'. It initializes the object's data fields. It has the same name as the class and no return type.

questions.question: What happens if you don't define any constructor in a class?
options: Java provides a default no-arg constructor
All fields are set to null
questions.explanation: If no constructor is defined, Java automatically provides a default no-arg constructor that initializes fields to their default values (0 for numbers, false for boolean, null for objects).
